svg.text: One session = one rooted DAG. ROOT connects turns; user/llm/code nodes share called_by edges and seq.
① One rooted graph: an actual session
ROOT connects three turns; turn 2 has nested wiki_agent calls, recursion, and loop siblings
Each user turn has called_by = ROOT (siblings under ROOT, not a chain)
Function for-loop: siblings under one parent (the loop is not a node)
Every node is reachable from ROOT along called_by: one connected tree. Within a turn, user → llm → function → llm nests; returns fill output without return edges.
② Context retrieval A: chat-level accumulation
No expose-based removal at chat level: prior chat remains visible.
② Context retrieval B: inside functions (scope exit)
Other function internals exit scope according to expose; io reveals only input/output by default
✗ Hidden from external context after return
Nodes remain for forks and visualization
Scope exit hides nodes from context without deletion. compute_reads accumulates chat; frame + expose apply within turns.
Design claim: one graph serves as both execution history and runtime context.
The source comparison describes other tools as observation-only or search-based, without this combination.
The claim concerns the integration, not individual components.
Chat stream (top-level messages; nested functions collapsed)
Call tree (expand called_by from ROOT; collapse loops as ×N)
